sbti_notes: NATIONAL RMBS TRUST 2022-1 is a Residential Mortgage-Backed Securities (RMBS) trust listed on ASX with code NRP. It is a securitization vehicle / financing trust structure that pools residential mortgages and issues securities to investors. As a pass-through entity with no operational business, it has no Scope 1 or 2 operational emissions. While the underlying mortgages may be originated by various Australian lenders (the "National" designation does not confirm a specific originating bank), the trust itself is not an operating company and therefore has no corporate climate targets. Any climate commitments would exist at the originating lender level, not at the trust level. The trust's GICS classification is listed as "Not Applic" on the ASX, consistent with its financing-vehicle status.

sbti_notes: NATIONAL RMBS TRUST 2024-1 is a Residential Mortgage-Backed Securities securitization trust issued by National Australia Bank Limited. It is a special purpose vehicle/financing subsidiary, not an operating company with independent climate targets. Parent company National Australia Bank Limited has corporate climate targets: Net zero by 2050 across financed and facilitated emissions and operations. Interim operational target: 72% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 (market-based) emissions by 2030 from 2022 baseline, updated in 2023 to align with 1.5°C scenario. NAB has also set twelve sectoral decarbonisation targets for 2030 including thermal coal to zero, power generation financing with 80% renewables (2025), and oil/gas reductions. NAB's targets are science-based (using SBTi methodology) but not formally SBTi-validated/approved.
notes: As an RMBS trust/securitization vehicle, NATIONAL RMBS TRUST 2024-1 has no independent operating entity climate targets. The trust pools residential mortgages and issues securities. Parent company National Australia Bank Limited's targets are the relevant corporate commitments. Confidence level set to "not_found" because the trust itself, as a financing vehicle/SPV, does not have standalone climate targets—it is a pass-through structure.

sbti_notes:
Transurban Finance Company Pty Ltd is a special purpose entity (SPE) and financing subsidiary of Transurban Group, used for debt issuance and capital raising. It is not an operating entity and therefore does not have independent climate targets. Parent company Transurban Group has the following validated targets: (1) 2030 Interim Targets (SBTi-validated): 50% absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions reduction from FY19 baseline; 22% reduction in carbon intensity of purchased goods and services (Scope 3, Category 1); 55% reduction in major projects emissions intensity (Scope 3, Category 2). (2) 2050 Net Zero Target (aligned with SBTi methodology but not formally validated as of June 2024): Net-zero GHG emissions across Scope 1, 2, and 3. Transurban met its 2030 targets in 2023, seven years early. First ASX20 company to have 2030 targets validated by SBTi.</sbti_notes>

target_description:
OWN OPERATIONS (Scope 1 & 2): Net zero emissions by FY2025. Achieved 98% reduction in Scopes 1 and 2 emissions since FY2020, with 100% renewable electricity for global offices and data centres. Scope 2 emissions reduced to zero since FY2022. Residual Scope 1 emissions offset with carbon removal units.

FINANCED EMISSIONS TARGETS (80% of balance sheet exposure to carbon-intensive sectors):

1. RESIDENTIAL MORTGAGES (FY2021 baseline):
   - Target: 11.6-19.3 kgCO2e/m² by 2030
   - Reduction: 50-70% from FY2021 baseline
   - Status: 33.2 kgCO2e/m² in FY2024 (14% reduction from FY2021)

2. OIL & GAS (FY2020 baseline):
   - Target: 56.3-59.6 gCO2e/MJ by 2030
   - Reduction: 9-14% from FY2020 baseline
   - Metric: Physical emissions intensity (Scope 1, 2, 3)

3. MOTOR VEHICLES (FY2020 baseline):
   - Target: 147 gCO2e/km by 2030
   - Reduction: 34% from FY2020 baseline
   - Metric: Physical emissions intensity (Scope 1, 2)

4. COAL SECTOR:
   - Limited equity and lending exposures were expected to run off by 2024

OVERALL FINANCED EMISSIONS COMMITMENT:
   - Net zero alignment by 2050 for financing activities
   - 2030 interim targets in place for high-emission sectors

SCOPE 3 (OWN OPERATIONS):
   - Measures and manages Scope 3 Categories 1-6 and 8
   - Category 6 (business travel) emissions offset with carbon offsets by 31 December 2025

target_description: 25% reduction in net Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from 2019 baseline
sbti_notes: Qantas has NOT obtained SBTi validation or registration. Research indicates Qantas set these targets independently and has not submitted them to the Science Based Targets initiative for formal validation. Climate Integrity noted that Qantas should set gross and intensity targets rather than 'net' emissions reduction targets to align with SBTi guidance.
notes: Base year 2019 with baseline of 12,493,616 mtCO2e. Target is for "net" emissions reduction relying on three pillars: (1) fleet and operational improvements including 1.5% average annual fuel efficiency improvement to 2030, (2) 10% sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) in fuel mix by 2030, and (3) carbon offsets/credits. No Scope 3 emissions reduction target has been set. Qantas established a AUD$400 million Climate Fund to support investments. Additional target: ~60% SAF in fuel mix by 2050. Note: Target relies significantly on carbon offsets in third pillar; critics note this is a "net" rather than absolute reduction target.

sbti_notes:
This is a residential mortgage-backed securities (RMBS) securitization trust - a special purpose vehicle that pools residential mortgages. As a financing subsidiary/trust structure (not an operating company), it does not set its own emissions targets. The Climate Bonds Initiative has a DNV GL Pre-Issuance Verification Statement (December 18, 2017) indicating the trust may meet climate bond criteria, but this relates to the underlying mortgages' green characteristics, not entity-level targets.
